answer.location_description: Top edge of the image, right of centre: roughly rows 0-2, columns 15-21, a band along the top border away from the nodule.
answer.shortcut_type: bright artifact/marker band at top border (non-anatomical, position-specific)
answer.mechanism: Several layer-1 units that otherwise vote malignant (units 19, 23, 10, 16, plus weaker 12 and 30) share a concentrated block of strongly negative weights over rows 0-2, cols ~15-21. Bright pixels there switch these units off, which removes their positive contribution to the logit. Through layer 2 (u4, u8, u13, u15 positive output weights; u0, u7, u9, u12 negative), units 10 and 16 net strongly positive, and unit 19 nets mildly positive. Several benign-voting centre-surround units (0, 8, 25, 5, 24, 31, 18) carry positive weights in the same top region. A bright patch there therefore pushes the output toward benign.
answer.evidence: The negative weights are much larger than the typical off-centre weights in these units. Unit 19, r0-r2 cols 14-21: -49, -58, -72, -69, -59 ... -70, -64. Unit 23, r0-r2 cols 16-21: -41 to -60. Unit 16, r0-r2 cols 15-21: -39, -37, -40, -47, -55. Unit 10, r0-r2: -41, -32, -40, -45, -52. These negatives sit at the image border, far from the nodule, and are asymmetric: the matching bottom and left borders are positive or neutral. Benign-leaning units are positive in the same zone: unit 0 r0 c20-21 = 33, 43; unit 8 r3 c20 = 49; unit 25 r0 c20 = 41. Approximate pathway contributions through W2 and W3: unit 16 is strongly positive (malignant), as is unit 10; unit 19 is mildly positive. Real lung anatomy would not produce a consistent top-border-only pattern shared across many units.
answer.main_feature: Centre-surround detectors at the nodule centre (rows ~10-16, cols ~9-15). A small compact bright core with a dark lung ring (units 0, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, ...) drives the output benign. A larger or irregular bright mass, where brightness extends into the surrounding ring and dims the centre (units 9, 10, 16, 6, 30, 12), drives it malignant.
